text:
Kaiden Guhle has been written up lately as a leader on the Canadiens' blue line, and he's playing like one in the physical sense: almost 23 minutes a night, 41 hits and 30 blocked shots in 16 games. He's missed four of Montreal's games, and Arpon Basu of The Athletic has written about how different the team looks when he's paired with Mike Matheson, who is now hurt.

The territorial numbers are the concern. Montreal takes only 43% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with Guhle on the ice, more than 10 points worse than without him, and 45% of the shot attempts. The goal results have hidden it: the Canadiens have scored 7.7 more goals than expected during his shifts. That's the kind of gap that closes, and when it does, the results around him won't look as kind.

There's a reason Montreal trusts him anyway. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 18% of the entries aimed at him last season, against 11% for a typical defenseman. That's real defending at the line. Our talent range expects about 7 goals. Without Matheson, watch who he plays with and whether the chances against come down.
